newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end sharply down on Greenspan remarks.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end sharply down on Greenspan remarks.

text.p: Brazil shares pared losses but still ended sharply down 2.42 percent as investors remained bearish following U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks on the U.S. economy.
"Greenspan's comments suggested that inflation is rising and interest rates should be raised and this is likely to hurt stock markets worldwide," a trader at a foreign bank said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most traded shares ended down 2,212 points at 89,279 points after falling to 88,102 points earlier. Turnover was high at 742.3 million reais ($706.1 million).

Speaking before the Senate Banking Committee, Greenspan questioned the sustainability of the U.S. stock market's sharp rise, adding that the central bank may have to raise U.S. interest rates in anticipation of inflation.

Brokers said the market was likely to keep moving sideways on Thursday while it continued to digest Greenspan's remarks. However, analysts noted that some investors took advantage of the profit-taking to buy stocks at a cheaper price.
"Although Greenspan's remarks had an immediate negative impact on the market, medium- and long-term prospects for Brazilian stocks are still very good mainly due to privatizations," an analyst said.
Bellwether Telebras preferred shares closed at 103.60 reais, down three percent. Mining giant Vale do Rio Doce preferred shares fell 2.46 percent to end at 27.80 reais.
Power utility Eletrobras preferred shares dropped 2.46 percent to close at 476 reais, while oil monopoly Petrobras preferred shares ended at 216 reais, down 2.7 percent.
Private mining firm Paranapanema fell 2.87 percent to end at 10.49 reais on news that the company lost its option to purchase Peruvian polymetallic unit Empresa Minera Yaulyacu.
The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index of the nine most liquid power shares fell 1.09 percent to end at 2,601 points.
